input: Watch a documentary series on astrophysics

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Astrophysics is broad — the series could cover cosmology, black holes, the Big Bang, exoplanets, or the full universe. Knowing the specific sub-topic changes which series to recommend.
Whether this is for solo watching, with a partner, family, or kids changes the appropriate complexity level and tone of the series.
The streaming platforms the user has access to (Netflix, Disney+, YouTube, etc.) directly determines which series are actually available to them.
Some viewers want cinematic visuals, others prefer lecture-style deep dives, others want a charismatic host — style preference filters recommendations significantly.
A background knowledge level (complete beginner vs. science-literate) determines whether to recommend an accessible popular series or a more technical one.
The goal — pure entertainment, learning fundamentals, or going deep on a specific concept — changes what 'done well' looks like and which series to prioritise.
Knowing how many episodes or hours they want to commit to shapes whether to recommend a short 4-episode series or a sprawling 13-episode run.

gold.taskDescription: The user wants to watch a documentary series focused on astrophysics, but the right series and approach depend on several unknowns about their background, preferences, and viewing context.

questions.title: Which astrophysics topic interests you most right now?
questions.description: Find out if the user is drawn to a specific sub-topic such as black holes, cosmology, the Big Bang, dark matter, exoplanets, or wants a broad overview of the universe.

questions.title: Will you be watching alone or with others?
questions.description: Determine whether the viewing audience is solo, a partner, family, or children, as this affects the appropriate complexity and tone of the recommended series.

questions.title: Which streaming platforms do you currently have access to?
questions.description: Identify available platforms (Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime, YouTube, PBS, etc.) to ensure the recommended series can actually be watched.

questions.title: Do you prefer a hosted show or pure narrated visuals?
questions.description: Establish whether the user wants a charismatic on-screen presenter (like Neil deGrasse Tyson or Brian Cox), a narrated visual documentary, or an interview/lecture style.

questions.title: How familiar are you with astrophysics concepts already?
questions.description: Gauge the user's existing knowledge level — complete beginner, casually curious, or science-literate — to calibrate the complexity of the recommendation.

questions.title: Is your main goal entertainment, learning, or both?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user prioritises cinematic spectacle and wonder, structured learning of concepts, or an equal blend of both, which determines the right series to prioritise.

questions.title: How many total hours are you willing to commit?
questions.description: Find out if the user wants a short, focused series (2–4 hours) or is happy to invest in a long multi-season run (10+ hours), shaping which series fit their schedule.
